item.description:
• Point at a workout to see its watts. Hover the shape of any workout — in the library, while riding, in the builder — and the block under the pointer shows its watts for you, % of FTP, zone, length, when it starts, its cadence and which rep of a set it is.
  • A workout's whole page. Click a workout's shape or name in the library: its figures, every block in your watts (a set as "3 ×"), its minutes in each zone, and the times you rode it. Rename and Load are there too, and on the card's right-click menu.
  • Find workouts by zone. The library's new zone menu shows only the workouts with Endurance, Threshold or VO₂max minutes, the most first; the filter now also finds a workout by its file name.
  • Sweet Spot and Zone 2 families. 23 new workouts. Sweet Spot from 30 minutes to 90 (2 × 8 up to 3 × 20 and 2 × 30), and five more ways to ride the 3 × 12: in steps (88–91–94%), with surges, with cadence changes, as over-unders, and as a pyramid or a countdown. Zone 2 from 45 minutes to two hours, plus a cadence pyramid, spin-ups, low cadence, waves, tempo touches and a fast finish. The library now shelves workouts by family, shortest first, and a sweet spot block is called that on hover.
  • A workout added mid-journey. Riding a journey on your gears, + WORKOUT beside the mode (top left, also in the menu) puts a workout on the road from that moment: ERG holds its watts and you ride on along the journey, rest stops and sights as before. When it is done you are back on your gears.
  • Journeys: a day counts only in a saving point. Stop anywhere you did not choose Rest here (or a detour's town) and the day is lost — it used to keep 90 %. A stop you did not choose (a shutdown, the trainer gone) still keeps everything, and the journey page's Saving points switch still turns the rule off. Before every start, the journey page and the start line say how far the next saving point is, how much climbing, and how long at your Z2 — the Bonette: 48.9 km, 1,592 m up, about 2 h 40 at 208 W.
  • Freiburg – Nice: places to stop on the passes. 26 hotels, refuges and restaurants on the long stretches between villages are saving points now (a bed on the journey card), from the Bonette's Halte 2000, Restefond and Camp des Fourches to the Refuge Napoléon on the Izoard and the Col du Glandon's restaurant — nowhere on the road is more than 25 km from a place to rest.
  • The zone rings fill while you collect. With no weekly target set, a ring stayed empty even while you collected minutes in it; it now fills against the goal you are collecting.

• Journeys. A new page (⌘0, and a tile on Home): one long real road ridden a day at a time, as many sessions as you like, until you arrive. The first is Freiburg – Nice, 900 km over 24 passes, from the Black Forest through the Jura and Gruyère to Mont Blanc, the Route des Grandes Alpes and the Cime de la Bonette, and down to the sea. Each session starts where the last one ended; ride it on your gears or with any workout in ERG. The road's heights come from laser surveys in Switzerland and France.
  • Saving points. The journey card offers where to rest tonight: the next villages and the next town. Press Rest here, ride to its marker in the 3D world, and the ride ends there by itself with the whole day kept. End the ride anywhere else and you keep 90 % of the day's distance, never less than the last town you passed (switch it off on the journey's page); End ride says which before you confirm, and a stop you did not choose (a shutdown, the trainer gone) keeps everything.
  • Detours. A town up to 10 km off the road can be a day's end: Go on the journey card turns off to it, the ride ends when you arrive, and the next day rides back to the road first.
  • 57 sights. Castles, cathedrals, lakes, glaciers, passes and the landmarks of Nice: as you come to one, the camera flies round it for a few seconds while you keep riding, with a photo and a few words on a card. They come at least twenty minutes apart, so a ride is never a string of them; V shows one again, and the ride menu can show each again when you reach it.
  • Postcards. Every sight you have ridden past is a postcard on the journey's page: its photo, the day you saw it and a link to Wikipedia.

• Minutes in zone this week. Home and Progress show how many minutes you have ridden this week, Monday to Sunday, in Endurance (zones 2–3) and VO₂max (zones 5–6), as small batteries that fill towards a weekly target of your own. Set the targets in Settings (⌘,), where Anifora suggests your average of the last four weeks; Threshold (zone 4) can be switched on there too. Every ride you have saved counts already; demo rides never do.
  • …and during the ride. With a target set, small rings after the mode at the top left fill with the week's minutes, this ride's part bright. Click them for the whole week. A card comes for a few seconds when a zone starts counting, another tenth of a target fills or a target is reached. Switch both off in the ride menu (Esc) or in Settings.
  • Collect minutes in a ride. Click the rings, then Collect minutes this ride under a zone: choose the minutes (they start at what your week still misses, spread over the days left) and collect them on your gears, or press Hold it for me: ERG holds the middle of Z2 for Endurance or Z4 for Threshold (± moves it inside the zone), and VO₂max comes as 4-minute reps with 3 minutes easy between. A capsule beside the mode shows how far along you are; click it or the rings to change or stop the goal. When the minutes are in, a card says so and the ride goes back to your gears.
  • What fills your week. Each workout in the library says how many of your week's missing minutes it would fill, zone by zone, and the order Fills my week puts the best fits first. Home names the one that fills most, with a Load button.
  • Try it on the demo trainer. A demo ride has a demo week of its own, with its own targets, so the rings, the cards and Collect can all be tried without real riding. It is never saved and never counts towards your own week.
